## Answer

Every other search hit (the genus-*p* dynamical-systems paper 0706.2397, the growth-and-mixing paper 0706.0954, etc.) is a semantic false positive — none of them treats diffeomorphism invariants as a topic. So the complete answer draws from this single paper.

The paper answers a 1954 question of Hirzebruch: **which linear combinations of Chern numbers of smooth complex projective varieties are diffeomorphism invariants of the underlying manifold?** The results are organized by complex dimension.

### Complex surfaces (dimension 2): both Chern numbers are invariant
For complex surfaces the two Chern numbers c₂ and c₁² *are* diffeomorphism invariants, and not even orientation-preservation is needed (p. 1).
- **Theorem 1**: If two compact complex surfaces are diffeomorphic, their Chern numbers coincide (p. 2). The argument: c₂ is the Euler characteristic, and Wu's formula c₁² = 2e + p₁ makes c₁² invariant under orientation-preserving homotopy equivalences; Seiberg–Witten theory (Kotschick 1995) forces the signature to vanish in the orientation-reversing case, so the Chern numbers still agree (p. 2).
- This fails at the *homeomorphism* level: **Theorem 2** gives infinitely many pairs of simply connected projective algebraic surfaces Xᵢ, Yᵢ of non-zero signature that are orientation-reversing homeomorphic but not diffeomorphic, with different c₁² (via c₁²(Yᵢ) = 4e(Xᵢ) − c₁²(Xᵢ)) (p. 2). These surfaces are the building blocks for all the higher-dimensional counterexamples.

### Complex three-folds (dimension 3): only the Euler number survives
- **Proposition 1**: There are infinitely many pairs of projective algebraic three-folds Zᵢ, Tᵢ that are diffeomorphic (both orientation-preserving and orientation-reversing) yet have c₁c₂(Zᵢ) ≠ c₁c₂(Tᵢ) and c₁³(Zᵢ) ≠ c₁³(Tᵢ). They are built as Xᵢ × ℂP¹ and Yᵢ × ℂP¹ from the Theorem 2 surfaces (pp. 3–4).
- **Theorem 3**: The only linear combinations of the Chern numbers c₁³, c₁c₂, c₃ that are invariant under orientation-preserving diffeomorphisms of simply connected projective algebraic three-folds are the **multiples of the Euler characteristic c₃** (p. 4). The proof uses non-trivial ℂP¹-bundles (projectivized tangent bundles) to show c₁c₂ and c₁³ vary independently — the combination 3c₁c₂ − c₁³ differs between the manifolds M and N (p. 5).

- **Theorem 4**: For projective algebraic n-folds with n ≥ 3, the only individual Chern number cᵢ that is diffeomorphism-invariant is the Euler number cₙ (p. 6). The counterexamples admit orientation-reversing diffeomorphisms, so restricting to orientation-preserving maps does not rescue any other individual Chern number (p. 6).

Because the individual Chern numbers are not diffeomorphism invariants, the paper poses a weaker question: are they at least determined *up to finite ambiguity*? The paper notes it has no counterexample to finite ambiguity in the projective-algebraic case, though it is false for non-Kähler complex manifolds (p. 1).

|---|---|---|
| 2 | c₂ **and** c₁² (both) | Thm 1, p. 2 |
| 3 | only multiples of the Euler char. c₃ | Thm 3, p. 4 |
| n ≥ 3 (individual) | only the Euler number cₙ | Thm 4, p. 6 |
| 4 (combinations) | span of c₄, p₁², p₂ | Thm 5, p. 8 |
